10.1002_advs.202504721: The limitations of conventional conductive agents in lithium‐ion batteries, such as carbon black and graphite flakes, have driven the search for high‐performance alternatives. Carbon nanotubes (CNTs) and graphene offer exceptional conductivity and lower dosage requirements, but face challenges related to high costs and complex fabrication processes. Herein, we develop a facile and cost‐effective one‐step chemical vapor deposition (CVD) strategy to achieve ultrahigh‐yield CNT growth (7692.31%) on reduced graphene oxide (rGO), constructing a covalently integrated 3D CNT@rGO composite. When deployed as a conductive agent in LiFePO 4 cathodes, the 3D architecture establishes multidirectional conductive networks that facilitate unimpeded electron/ion transport during electrochemical reactions. This results in significantly enhanced rate capability across 1‐6 C rates and exceptional cycling stability with 96.32% capacity retention after 300 cycles at 1 C. The synergistic attributes—including multidimensional conduction pathways, minimal catalyst residue (0.52%), and homogeneous dispersion—collectively provide an efficient and economical solution for next‐generation battery technologies. This work paves the way for scalable battery technologies utilizing high‐performance carbon‐based conductive agents.
10.1002_advs.75418: Flexible supercapacitor (SC) represents a promising power source for wearable electronics, but its cycling and flexible stabilities are currently limited by the weak interaction at the electrode/electrolyte interface. We construct a covalent electrode/electrolyte interface by anchored interfacial polymerization and a topologically entangled electrolyte/electrolyte interface by in situ polymerization in one SC. The interfacial toughness and adhesion strength between electrode and electrolyte reach 2965.3 J m −2 and 241.6 kPa, respectively, which are two orders and one order of those assembled by the traditional stacking approach. The seamless interfaces efficiently promote ion transport ability among them, which provides the SC with a three‐time enhancement of specific capacitance, compared with the device by the DS method. The developed SC exhibits high capacitance retention of 89.5% for 10 5 charge/discharge cycles and 96.2% after folding for 10 5 times, indicating outstanding stability of structure and performance. The demonstrated seamless interfacial engineering can be easily expanded in the field of other flexible electronics.
10.1002_aenm.71732: Perovskite solar cells (PSCs) have achieved remarkable power conversion efficiency (PCE) recently, yet the device instability induced by defects remains a bottleneck. Despite the effectiveness of passivation strategies in reducing defects, conventional solution‐based methods may compromise the perovskite crystallinity. Thus, vapor‐based molecules are expected to penetrate into crystals and reduce defects. Screening effective vapor‐assisted passivation materials usually takes substantial trial‐and‐error costs. Here, we propose a hybrid workflow integrating machine learning models with first‐principles calculations to screen the key functional groups for vapor‐assisted passivation molecules and provide physical insights. The phenyl and halogen atoms were identified by Shapley additive explanation (SHAP) analysis to be effective. Theoretical calculations also indicated that there was a strong cation‐ π interaction between Pb 2+ and benzene ring. Besides, halogenated benzene could intercalate into the iodine vacancies on perovskite surfaces. Such robust interactions synergistically contribute to the stability of [PbI 6 ] 4− octahedral framework, and thus the formation of defects and structural collapse could be effectively suppressed. Moreover, the thermal conductivity of modified perovskite films was remarkably enhanced. Finally, the device modified with iodobenzene vapor achieved the champion PCE of 26.94%. This workflow integrating data‐driven discovery and atomistic understandings, provides an innovative strategy to screen vapor‐assisted passivation materials.
10.1016_j.jma.2026.102245: Magnesium alloys are increasingly attractive for marine applications due to their low density and high specific strength; however, their inherent susceptibility to corrosion and biofouling severely restricts long-term performance. The simultaneous integration of corrosion resistance, superhydrophobicity and antifouling qualities has been made possible by recent developments in multifunctional coating design. This review systematically summarizes the design strategies of magnesium-based composite coatings, including plasma electrolytic oxidation, sol-gel, hydrothermal and bioinspired hybrid systems with particular emphasis on their structure-property relationships. Special consideration is given to the synergistic interplay between micro/nano hierarchical architectures and low-surface-energy modifications, which collectively strengthen barrier performance, reduce wettability, and inhibit biological adhesion in marine environments. The novelty of this review lies in establishing a unified framework that correlates these functionalities, highlighting their interdependence rather than treating them as independent attributes. Furthermore, critical challenges related to coating durability, mechanical robustness and long-term stability under dynamic marine conditions are discussed. Finally, future perspectives are outlined for the development of smart, self-healing and environmentally sustainable coating systems for next-generation magnesium-based marine applications.
10.1016_j.watres.2026.125813: Organotin compounds, such as Tributyltin (TBT), pose significant environmental risks and threaten wildlife, food chain, and human health even years after being banned, highlighting the need for effective removal methods. The Nyex Rosalox™ (NR) process, a novel coupled adsorption and electrochemical oxidation technology, has shown success in removing various organic pollutants. However, its applicability to remove organometallic compounds remains unclear. Therefore, this study evaluated the effectiveness of TBT removal from water using the NR process and investigated the fate of tin and the formation of degradation products. Analyses showed that at high (50 mg/L) concentrations 62% to 71% TBT in fresh water and 73% to 86% in brackish water could be effectively removed in 1-hour using 6.5 W. The presence of NaCl enhanced conductivity and promoted hypochlorite formation, further improving TBT oxidation. Although direct electrochemical oxidation of TBT (i.e., without adsorption on Nyex™ media) was observed at high concentrations and elevated salinity, at low (0.5 mg/L) concentrations adsorption onto Nyex™ media played a crucial role in enhancing treatment efficiency and stability. No significant production of toxic degradation products such as monobutyltin and dibutyltin was observed, and up to 94% of the inorganic tin (Sn 4+ , the final oxidation product) formed, was immobilised on the Nyex™ media, but could be remobilised by rinsing with a weak acid solution. This is the first study to assess the fate of the inorganic component of an organometallic compound in a coupled adsorption and electrochemical oxidation treatment process. This work demonstrates that the NR process holds promise for treating other organometallic pollutants, potentially at even at lower organotin concentrations.
10.1039_d5ta06308f: High-entropy alloys (HEAs) are emerging electrocatalysts, which can convert inert Cu into a highly active electrocatalytic site by controlling the electronic structure of Cu through electronegativity differences after alloying.
